The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 piercing damage and stop moving. A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 piercing damage to the trapped creature.

sourceDescriptionClauses: Includes a backpack, a blanket, 10 candles, a tinderbox, an alms box, 2 blocks of incense, a censer, vestments, 2 days of rations, and a waterskin.

records.name: Quiver
sourceDescriptionClauses: Quiver. A quiver can hold up to 20 arrows.

records.name: Ram, portable
sourceDescriptionClauses: Ram, Portable. You can use a portable ram to break down doors. When doing so, you gain a +4 bonus on the Strength check. One other character can help you use the ram, giving you advantage on this check.

sourceBindings.phrase: gain a +4 bonus on the Strength check. One other character can help you use the ram, giving you advantage on this check

records.name: Rations (1 day)
sourceDescriptionClauses: Rations. Rations consist of dry foods suitable for extended travel, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts.

records.name: Reliquary
sourceDescriptionClauses: Holy Symbol. A holy symbol is a representation of a god or pantheon. It might be an amulet depicting a symbol representing a deity, the same symbol carefully engraved or inlaid as an emblem on a shield, or a tiny box holding a fragment of a sacred relic. Appendix PH-B "Fantasy-Historical Pantheons" lists the symbols commonly associated with many gods in the multiverse. A cleric or paladin can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus. To use the symbol in this way, the caster must hold it in hand, wear it visibly, or bear it on a shield.

records.name: Ring mail
sourceDescriptionClauses: Ring Mail. This armor is leather armor with heavy rings sewn into it. The rings help reinforce the armor against blows from swords and axes. Ring mail is inferior to chain mail, and it's usually worn only by those who can’t afford better armor.

records.name: Rod
sourceDescriptionClauses: Arcane Focus. An arcane focus is a special item— an orb, a crystal, a rod, a specially constructed staff, a wand-like length of wood, or some similar item— designed to channel the power of arcane spells. A sorcerer, warlock, or wizard can use such an item as a spellcasting focus.

records.name: Rope, hempen (50 feet)
sourceDescriptionClauses: Rope. Rope, whether made of hemp or silk, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

burst with a DC 17 Strength check

records.name: Scale mail
sourceDescriptionClauses: Scale Mail. This armor consists of a coat and leggings (and perhaps a separate skirt) of leather covered with overlapping pieces of metal, much like the scales of a fish. The suit includes gauntlets.

records.name: Scale, merchant’s
sourceDescriptionClauses: Scale, Merchant’s. A scale includes a small balance, pans, and a suitable assortment of weights up to 2 pounds. With it, you can measure the exact weight of small objects, such as raw precious metals or trade goods, to help determine their worth.

records.name: Scholar’s Pack
sourceDescriptionClauses: Includes a backpack, a book of lore, a bottle of ink, an ink pen, 10 sheets of parchment, a little bag of sand, and a small knife.

records.name: Shawm
sourceDescriptionClauses: Musical Instrument. Several of the most common types of musical instruments are shown on the table as examples. If you have proficiency with a given musical instrument, you can add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to play music with the instrument. A bard can use a musical instrument as a spellcasting focus. Each type of musical instrument requires a separate proficiency.

records.name: Smith’s tools
sourceDescriptionClauses: Artisan’s Tools. These special tools include the items needed to pursue a craft or trade. The table shows examples of the most common types of tools, each providing items related to a single craft. Proficiency with a set of artisan’s tools lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make using the tools in your craft. Each type of artisan’s tools requires a separate proficiency.

records.name: Spellbook
sourceDescriptionClauses: Spellbook. Essential for wizards, a spellbook is a leather-bound tome with 100 blank vellum pages suitable for recording spells.

records.name: Splint
sourceDescriptionClauses: Splint. This armor is made of narrow vertical strips of metal riveted to a backing of leather that is worn over cloth padding. Flexible chain mail protects the joints.

records.name: Sprig of mistletoe
sourceDescriptionClauses: Druidic Focus. A druidic focus might be a sprig of mistletoe or holly, a wand or scepter made of yew or another special wood, a staff drawn whole out of a living tree, or a totem object incorporating feathers, fur, bones, and teeth from sacred animals. A druid can use such an object as a spellcasting focus.

records.name: Spyglass
sourceDescriptionClauses: Spyglass. Objects viewed through a spyglass are magnified to twice their size.

records.name: Staff
sourceDescriptionClauses: Arcane Focus. records.name: Studded leather
sourceDescriptionClauses: Studded Leather. Made from tough but flexible leather, studded leather is reinforced with close-set rivets or spikes.

records.name: Tent, two-person
sourceDescriptionClauses: Tent. A simple and portable canvas shelter, a tent sleeps two.

records.name: Thieves’ tools
sourceDescriptionClauses: Thieves’ Tools. This set of tools includes a small file, a set of lock picks, a small mirror mounted on a metal handle, a set of narrow-bladed scissors, and a pair of pliers. Proficiency with these tools lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to disarm traps or open locks.

records.name: Tinderbox
sourceDescriptionClauses: Tinderbox. This small container holds flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a torch—or anything else with abundant, exposed fuel—takes an action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.

records.name: Torch
sourceDescriptionClauses: Torch. A torch burns for 1 hour, providing bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a burning torch and hit, it deals 1 fire damage.
